title: Three rounds of regression on a 50-question exam: 0.82 → 0.88 (regression caught) → 0.94

events.label: Build the 50-question set
events.detail: Three sources: 30 real tickets, 12 edge cases, 8 adversarial cases; every question carries a golden answer and a class label (returns / billing / inquiry).

events.label: v1 batch run
events.detail: Current prompt version v1; all 50 questions pass through the system — the evaluation set behaves like an ordinary user.

events.label: 50 answers collected
events.detail: Three scoring methods stand ready: exact match, rule validation, LLM-as-judge.

events.label: v1 scored
events.detail: Exact match governs field values, rule validation governs format and length, semantic equivalence goes to the LLM judge — the judge is also a model, and its bias needs human-sampling calibration.

events.label: v1 total 0.82
events.detail: Overall pass rate 41/50 = 0.82; by class: returns 0.9, billing 0.75, inquiry 0.8 — billing is the weak leg.

events.label: Prompt revised to v2
events.detail: Two few-shot examples added for the billing class (P02's move) — change only this one thing and keep the comparison.

events.label: v2 full re-run
events.detail: The discipline of regression testing: not just the changed billing class — all 50 questions re-run, because the prompt is a global variable.

events.label: v2's 50 answers collected
events.detail: Same scorer, same rules — otherwise the two rounds' scores are not comparable.

events.label: v2 scored
events.detail: Total 44/50 = 0.88: billing 0.75→0.9 meets target, but returns 0.9→0.7 — one score rose while the other fell.

events.label: The regression diff catches a regression
events.detail: Total 0.82→0.88 rose, yet the returns class dropped 20 points — an evaluation that reads only the total lets this regression walk; metrics must be layered (overall + by class).

events.label: Locate and fix the cause
events.detail: Question-by-question diff: returns answers lost the required field 'return method' — the new billing examples' format got imitated by the returns class. A trap hidden in the examples (P02's lesson).

events.label: v3 re-run
events.detail: The examples' format trap fixed (required fields completed inside the examples); third full re-run.

events.label: v3 all green, delivered
events.detail: Total 47/50 = 0.94, all three classes ≥0.9. The report is layered: overall pass rate plus per-class error distribution — regressions have nowhere left to hide.
